traceability.evidence:
Story file docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md exists and is referenced throughout the maintenance code and tests.
Implementation of requirements: - REQ-MAINT-DETECT: - Implemented by detectStaleAnnotations in src/maintenance/detect.ts. It: - Resolves a workspace root from the provided path (process.cwd() + codebasePath). - Returns [] when the directory does not exist or is not a directory. - Recursively scans files (via getAllFiles) and parses @story annotations. - Skips unsafe/invalid story paths using isUnsafeStoryPath and enforces project boundaries via enforceProjectBoundary. - Marks story paths as stale only when no in-project candidate exists on disk. - Tested by: - tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts: no-stale case and detection of a stale story file. - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts: non-existent directory returns [], nested directories detection, behavior on permission errors, and security validation that malicious or out-of-project paths are not stat()'d.
- REQ-MAINT-UPDATE: - Implemented by updateAnnotationReferences in src/maintenance/update.ts. It: - Returns 0 early if the codebase path does not exist or is not a directory. - Builds a regex matching "@story " and walks all files via getAllFiles. - For each file, processFileForAnnotationUpdates updates only @story occurrences from oldPath to newPath, increments a replacement counter, and writes the file only if content changed. - Tested by: - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts: returns 0 when no updates are made. - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts: correctly updates @story old.path.md to new.path.md and returns count 1; returns 0 for non-existent directories.
- REQ-MAINT-BATCH and REQ-MAINT-VERIFY: - Implemented in src/maintenance/batch.ts: - batchUpdateAnnotations(root, mappings) loops over mappings and sums updateAnnotationReferences results. - verifyAnnotations(root) calls detectStaleAnnotations(root) and returns stale.length === 0. - Tested by tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts: - batchUpdateAnnotations returns 0 when no mappings. - verifyAnnotations returns true when annotations are valid and the referenced story file exists.
- REQ-MAINT-REPORT: - Implemented by generateMaintenanceReport in src/maintenance/report.ts: - Calls detectStaleAnnotations(root). - Returns an empty string when there are no stale annotations; otherwise returns a newline-separated list of stale story paths. - Tested by tests/maintenance/report.test.ts: - Returns "" when no stale entries. - Contains the missing story name when a stale annotation is present.
- REQ-MAINT-SAFE (safety, reversibility, clear behavior): - Core helpers: - detectStaleAnnotations handles missing roots and file read failures safely (returning [] or skipping unreadable files) and uses security checks before touching the filesystem. - updateAnnotationReferences returns 0 without changes when the root does not exist and only writes files when necessary. - CLI layer (src/maintenance/cli.ts and src/maintenance/commands.ts): - Defines exit codes EXIT_OK (0), EXIT_STALE (1), EXIT_USAGE (2). - runMaintenanceCli normalizes args, dispatches to detect/verify/report/update, prints help when no subcommand or when -h/--help is used, and wraps dispatch in a try/catch that prints "traceability-maint failed: " to stderr and exits with EXIT_USAGE on unexpected errors. - handleDetect/handleVerify/handleReport/handleUpdate all provide clear text or JSON outputs and stable exit codes; handleUpdate enforces required --from/--to flags and supports a non-destructive --dry-run mode that does not modify files and instead estimates impact. - Tested by tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts: - Detect: clean workspace exits 0 with "No stale @story annotations found."; --json outputs a JSON object with stale list and exits 1 when stale annotations exist; non-existent --root exits 0 and prints the no-stale message. - Verify: exits 0 and logs once when annotations are valid. - Report: prints a Markdown-style human-readable report including a header and stale story name, exits 0; invalid --format (e.g., yaml) causes exit code 2 and a clear error mentioning valid values. - Update: performs replacements and exits 0; missing --from/--to exits 2 with an error and help; --dry-run exits 0, prints that no files were modified, and confirms the file content did not change. - Safety: calling CLI with no subcommand prints help and exits 0 without errors; a simulated EACCES from fs.statSync in detect leads to exit code 2 with an error message prefixed by "traceability-maint failed:".
Integration and exposure: - src/maintenance/index.ts exports detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport, and is annotated with this story and its REQ-MAINT-* requirements. - src/index.ts imports these and exposes them via a maintenance export and via plugin.maintenance; this file is annotated with @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and @req REQ-MAINTENANCE-API-EXPORT. - tests/maintenance/index.test.ts verifies that all maintenance functions are exported as functions. - package.json includes a bin entry: "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js", wiring the CLI binary required by the story.
Documentation and user experience: - README.md, section "Maintenance CLI" (lines 108–143), documents: - The purpose of the traceability-maint CLI. - The four subcommands (detect, verify, report, update) and their responsibilities. - Concrete usage examples including detection, verification, JSON reporting, and updating references when a story file is renamed. - user-docs/api-reference.md, section "Maintenance API and CLI" (lines 234–520), documents: - Programmatic API: detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport (parameters, return values, behavior notes). - CLI options (--root, --json, --format, --from, --to, --dry-run, --help) and exit codes (0, 1, 2). - Expected human-readable and JSON outputs for detect, report, and update (including dry-run JSON shape). - Safety posture (local filesystem only, no network, clear exit codes), aligning with REQ-MAINT-SAFE.
Tests and CI evidence: - Running `npm test -- --verbose` completes successfully with all Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS tests passing. Jest output shows PASS for: - tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - tests/maintenance/report.test.ts - tests/maintenance/index.test.ts - tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts - Overall Jest summary: 35 test suites passed, 266 tests passed.
Traceability: - All relevant implementation files (src/maintenance/*.ts, src/index.ts, src/maintenance/cli.ts, src/maintenance/commands.ts) and tests under tests/maintenance/*.test.ts contain @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and @req REQ-MAINT-* annotations, explicitly linking each piece of behavior back to this story.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria of docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md are satisfied: - Core Functionality: Detection and update operations are implemented (detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport) and exposed both programmatically and via the traceability-maint CLI. - Quality Standards: Maintenance functions operate via focused text replacements on @story paths, only write files when content changes, and never touch @req annotations. Tests confirm correct behavior on empty, nested, and non-existent directories, indicating non-destructive operation. - Integration: Maintenance utilities are exposed through src/index.ts as plugin.maintenance and integrated into the tooling ecosystem via a bin entry for the CLI. They reuse existing validation/file utilities (e.g., storyReferenceUtils) from other stories. - User Experience: The CLI provides clear, human-readable messages and structured JSON outputs; README.md and user-docs/api-reference.md both document commands, options, and example invocations. - Error Handling: Functions and CLI commands handle missing roots, invalid options, permission errors (simulated in tests), and unsafe paths in a controlled way, using explicit exit codes and clear error messages. - Documentation: The maintenance API and CLI are documented in both README.md and user-docs/api-reference.md with usage examples and behavior notes. An ADR (docs/decisions/adr-maintenance-cli-interface.md) describes the CLI design and matches the implementation. Given the implemented code, exhaustive tests tied to this story, passing test run, and comprehensive documentation, the story is fully implemented.
